architecture: Client-side single-page React application. Zero backend, zero build in the live reader. Single shared source ('the brain') consumed by two independent shells (no-build browser loader + Vite build). Static content modules, layered CSS token system, fixed-canvas uniform scaling instead of responsive reflow.

layers.note: Two readers + the CDN runtime they resolve React and JSX through.

plain.label: How it starts up
plain.note: The two ways the app can be opened, plus the helpers it borrows from the internet.

layers.label: Entry
layers.note: The one mount point both shells reach.

plain.label: The front door
plain.note: The first file that runs. Both ways in arrive here.

plain.label: The conductor
plain.note: Remembers which screen you are on and sets the app-wide look.

layers.label: Screens
layers.note: Fixed-canvas tray screens ported from the Design Lab study.

plain.label: The screens
plain.note: The three tile screens, each drawn at a fixed size and scaled to fit.

layers.label: UI Primitives
layers.note: Reusable components, icons, figures, tweak controls.

plain.label: Reusable pieces
plain.note: Parts used all over: navigation, tiles, icons, diagrams.

layers.label: Static Data
layers.note: Compiled-in constants. No API, no database.

plain.label: The content
plain.note: The lessons and artwork, typed into the app. Nothing is fetched.

layers.label: Style Cascade
layers.note: One stylesheet entry that @imports an ordered chain.

plain.label: The look
plain.note: Six stylesheets loaded in a fixed order. Later ones can overrule earlier ones.

nodes.label: index.html
nodes.notes: Links the brain's single stylesheet, declares the import map, paints the phone gate + boot placeholder, then hands off to the loader. Holds no app logic.

plain.sub: the live product — double-click and it runs
plain.notes: The page you actually open. It holds no app code: it loads the look, shows a placeholder so the screen is never blank, and hands off to the loader.

nodes.label: zmath-loader
nodes.notes: Babel-standalone only compiles the script tag it owns, so this walks the import graph itself: fetch each relative module, transform JSX, rewrite relative specifiers to blob URLs, pin import.meta.url, dynamic-import the entry. Bare specifiers pass through to the import map untouched.

plain.sub: reads your raw files and translates them
plain.notes: The app’s code is written in a dialect browsers do not understand. This walks through every file, fetches it, translates it, and rewires its references to its neighbours — so there is no publishing step. Save and refresh is the whole loop.

nodes.label: @babel/standalone
nodes.notes: JSX → JS in the browser. Only needed by the no-build reader; Vite does this at build time.

plain.sub: the translator, fetched from the internet
plain.notes: Converts the source dialect into something the browser can run. Only the live version needs it; the packaged build does this ahead of time.

nodes.label: esm.sh · React 18.3.1
nodes.notes: The import map maps the same bare specifiers ('react', 'react-dom/client') that Vite resolves — which is exactly why one set of source files runs in both readers.

plain.sub: the app toolkit, fetched from the internet
plain.notes: React, the toolkit the app is built with. Both ways of opening the app ask for it by the same name — which is exactly why one set of files works in both.

nodes.label: index.html
nodes.notes: Standard Vite host page. Loads src/main.jsx as a module.

plain.notes: A plain host page for the packaged build. Nothing of the app lives here.

nodes.label: src/main.jsx
nodes.notes: Contains no app source. Imports the brain's styles.css and the brain's main.jsx from the sibling folder. Vite follows the graph, so dist/ is self-contained.

plain.notes: Points at the brain: one line for the look, one for the app. This is what makes the packaged build a reader rather than a copy.

nodes.label: vite.config.js
nodes.notes: base: '/alphabetmath/' for GitHub Pages; server.fs.allow ['..'] so the dev server may serve the sibling brain folder.

plain.notes: Tells the packager where the app will live online, and gives it permission to read the brain folder next door.

nodes.label: main.jsx
nodes.notes: createRoot(#root) renders <App/> wrapped in an ErrorBoundary that prints the real stack instead of a blank screen. Also sets document.title — the brain owns shell chrome so neither shell needs it.

plain.notes: Ten lines. Starts the app and wraps it in a safety net that prints a real error instead of a blank white screen.

nodes.label: app.jsx
nodes.notes: Holds page state (Home/Topics/Projects/Notes/About) and swaps components from a screens map — no router. Owns the modal entry state, the tweak state, the resize→--ipad-scale/--hd-scale effect, and the effect that writes data-ambience/-material/-fit/-tilemat/-traymat onto <html>. Optional ?page= and ?fit= URL overrides.

plain.notes: Remembers which screen you are on and swaps them like changing channels; the address bar never moves. Also owns the pop-up panel and writes the app-wide appearance switches.

nodes.label: picker-screens.jsx
nodes.notes: 980×612 logical canvas scaled with useFit (min(w/980, h/612) capped at 1.6×). Tiles 218×162, cartridges 294×162. TRAY-CONTAINMENT RULE: tiles are direct children of .scr so tray + tiles scale as one unit. Lab tap rhythm: first tap rings, second opens. Arrow-key navigation.

plain.notes: Drawn once at a fixed size and scaled to fit your window like a photo — nothing rearranges. The tiles sit inside the tray so both scale as one unit. Tap once to select, twice to open.

nodes.label: lab-screen.jsx
nodes.notes: The Projects screen: spotlight cartridge rail on the same fixed-canvas scaling recipe. Selected cartridge calls onOpen({type:'project'}) into the shared modal.

plain.notes: A spotlight rail of cartridges. This screen came first; Home and Topics were modelled on it.

nodes.label: components.jsx
nodes.notes: Navigation rail, tiles, the shared modal, note article blocks and reader, PixelLetter brand mark. Registers its own 'parallelogram' figure into ZFIGURES and imports figures.jsx purely for its registration side-effect.

plain.notes: Pieces used all over: the side navigation, the tiles, the pop-up panel, the note reader, the pixel logo.

nodes.label: icons.jsx
nodes.notes: Inline SVG path table; three finishes (line, glossy glyph, capsule badge) driven by props rather than separate assets.

plain.notes: Icons are drawn by code rather than stored as image files, so one icon can appear in three finishes without drawing it three times.

nodes.label: tweaks-panel.jsx
nodes.notes: Design-time control surface. useTweaks holds values; setTweak persists by asking the host to rewrite the EDITMODE block in app.jsx on disk. Self-injecting stylesheet, so it drops into any page.

plain.notes: A control panel for adjusting the look without editing code. A tool for building the app, not a feature of it. Choices are saved back into the source.

nodes.label: figures.jsx
nodes.notes: Generative SVG diagrams for note articles. Each registers itself into the shared ZFIGURES object — imported for side-effect, never called directly.

plain.notes: Illustrations drawn by code, so they stay sharp at any size. Each one hangs itself on the shared hook when the app starts.

nodes.label: figkit.jsx
nodes.sub: DETACHED — not in the runtime graph
nodes.notes: Reusable figure primitives (lattice/area widgets, paper controls). Converted to ESM during the migration but nothing imports it — it does not load at runtime. Either wire it into figures.jsx or retire it.

plain.notes: A box of reusable diagram parts that nothing refers to. It never loads and has no effect on the app. It looks alive, which wastes a future reader’s time — wire it in or delete it.

nodes.label: data.js
nodes.notes: ZMATH_TOPICS, ZMATH_PROJECTS, ZMATH_NOTES (article bodies + exercises inline), ZMATH_HOME mosaic spec, NOTE_GLYPH palettes, plus derived ById lookup maps. Content is compiled in, never fetched.

plain.notes: The book itself: all the content typed straight into the app. Adding a lesson means editing this file. Nothing is fetched from a server.

nodes.label: tile-covers.js
nodes.notes: Registry of composed SVG cover art keyed by topic id (tile / cart / art variants). injectComposedDefs() writes one hidden <defs> block into the document; every cover is then a lightweight <use href> reference.

plain.notes: Cover art stored once and referred to wherever it appears, instead of copied per tile.

nodes.label: figures-registry.js
nodes.notes: One exported object that figures.jsx and components.jsx populate and NoteBlock reads. Replaced the old window.ZFIGURES global so the import graph has a single well-defined owner with no load-order dependence.

plain.notes: A shared list. Diagrams hang themselves up by name when the app starts; articles collect them by name. Neither side needs to know about the other, and nothing depends on load order.

nodes.label: styles.css
nodes.notes: Both shells load exactly this file. Order is the contract: tokens → app → flat-composed → lab → picker → tweaks-overrides. New sheets are added here, never in a shell.

plain.sub: the one stylesheet both ways load
plain.notes: Pulls in five others in a deliberate order. New styling goes on this list, never onto a page — otherwise the two versions would look different.

nodes.label: tokens.css
nodes.notes: Color, type, spacing and material variables — the base every later sheet reads.

plain.notes: Named values everything else refers to. Change one here and it changes everywhere.

nodes.label: app.css
nodes.notes: Shell layout, sidebar, stage, modal, notes reader, and the pure-CSS rotate guard rule body:has(#rotate-guard) #root{display:none}.

plain.notes: Navigation, stage, pop-ups, the note reader — plus the rule that hides the app when the tablet is held the wrong way.

nodes.label: flat-composed.css
nodes.notes: The flat molded tile look — THE material since Phase 5 (the shiny variant was retired).

plain.notes: The flat moulded look of the tiles. The shiny alternative was retired.

nodes.label: lab.css
nodes.notes: Scoped under .lab-spot. Owns the base tile material and the cartridge rail that Home/Topics also inherit from.

plain.notes: Owns the base tile look and the cartridge rail that Home and Topics inherit.

nodes.label: picker.css
nodes.notes: Shelves and grid trays, capsule heads, ghost art, corner badges. Also scoped under .lab-spot.

plain.notes: Shelves, grid, labels, badges. Tile sizes are fixed numbers here — the sliver of the next tile you see at full width falls out of those numbers, and tells you there is more to scroll to without needing an arrow.

nodes.label: tweaks-overrides.css
nodes.notes: Reacts to the data-* attributes App writes on <html>. Loaded last so it wins.

plain.notes: Watches for the appearance switches and restyles accordingly. Being last means it can overrule everything above.

flows.label: Boot — no-build (live product)
flows.summary: How index.html turns raw .jsx files on disk into a running React app with no build step.

steps.title: Shell paints first
steps.detail: styles.css is linked, the phone gate rule and the #zmath-boot placeholder render immediately so the page never flashes blank while modules download.

plain.title: The screen is never blank
plain.detail: The look loads first and a placeholder appears, so a slow start looks like loading rather than breakage.

steps.title: Babel standalone loads
steps.detail: Pinned 7.29.0 with an integrity hash. It is the only thing that can turn JSX into JS in this reader.

plain.title: The translator arrives
plain.detail: A small translator is fetched from the internet to turn the source dialect into something the browser can run.

steps.title: loadGraph walks the import graph
steps.detail: Starting at ./zmath/main.jsx it fetches the source, regex-collects every relative specifier, and recurses depth-first with a cache so each module is built once.

plain.title: The files are walked, one leading to the next
plain.detail: Starting from one file, the loader reads it, notices which other files it mentions, fetches those, and keeps going until everything is collected. Each file is fetched only once.

steps.title: Transform, rewrite, blob-ify
steps.detail: Each module is Babel-transformed, its relative imports are rewritten to the blob URLs of the already-built dependencies, and import.meta.url is pinned to the real file URL (a blob: URL is not a resolvable base).

plain.title: Each file is translated and rewired
plain.detail: Every file is converted, and its references to its neighbours are pointed at the already-translated copies held in memory. This is the fiddly part, and the price of having no build step.

steps.title: Bare specifiers fall through
steps.detail: 'react' and 'react-dom/client' are left untouched and resolved by the import map to esm.sh — the same specifiers Vite resolves, which is what keeps one source set valid for both readers.

plain.title: The toolkit is fetched
plain.detail: The toolkit’s names are left untouched and looked up on the internet — the same names the packaged build uses, which is why one set of files works both ways.

steps.title: Dynamic import of the entry blob
steps.detail: The finished blob URL is imported. main.jsx sets document.title and calls createRoot(#root).

plain.title: The app starts
plain.detail: The finished file is handed to the browser. The app takes over the page and the placeholder disappears.

steps.title: App mounts inside the ErrorBoundary
steps.detail: A render failure prints the real stack in monospace instead of a blank screen; a loader failure prints its own message into #root.

plain.title: With a safety net around it
plain.detail: If anything fails, the real error is printed on the page instead of a blank white screen.

plain.label: Opening the app (the live version)
plain.summary: How raw files on disk become a running app with no publishing step.

flows.label: Boot — Vite build (desktop app)
flows.summary: The second reader. Same brain files, resolved natively at build time instead of in the browser.

steps.title: Config points outward
steps.detail: server.fs.allow ['..'] lets the dev server read the sibling brain folder; base '/alphabetmath/' matches the GitHub Pages repo path.

plain.title: Settings point next door
plain.detail: Tells the packager where the app will live online, and gives it permission to read the brain folder.

steps.title: Vite host page loads src/main.jsx
steps.detail: A conventional Vite entry — no app markup of its own beyond #root.

plain.title: The host page loads
plain.detail: A plain page with nothing of the app in it.

steps.title: The thin reader imports the brain
steps.detail: Two lines: the brain's styles.css and the brain's main.jsx, both by relative path into '../../AlphabetMath - Mobile/zmath/'. No source is ever copied here.

plain.title: Two lines point at the brain
plain.detail: One line for the look, one for the app. No app code is ever copied here.

steps.title: Vite follows the CSS chain
steps.detail: styles.css @imports all six sheets in order, so the built bundle carries the identical cascade the no-build page gets.

plain.title: The look follows automatically
plain.detail: The one stylesheet pulls in all six, so the packaged version gets the identical look.

steps.title: Same entry, no Babel
steps.detail: Vite's React plugin compiled the JSX at build time; the loader and Babel-standalone are simply absent from this path.

plain.title: Same front door, no translator
plain.detail: Translation already happened during packaging, so the loader and the translator are simply absent from this path.

steps.title: Identical app, self-contained dist/
steps.detail: The build inlines the brain, so the shipped folder stands alone — the two readers cannot drift because there is only one copy of the source.

plain.title: Identical app, nothing borrowed
plain.detail: Everything is baked in, so it needs no internet at startup. The two versions cannot drift, because there is only one copy of the source.

plain.label: Opening the app (the packaged version)
plain.summary: The second way in. Same files, prepared ahead of time instead of translated on the spot.

flows.label: Navigation — rail → screen → modal
flows.summary: State-driven screen swapping. There is no router and no URL change.

steps.title: Sidebar rail click
steps.detail: Sidebar calls setPage(p) and scrolls .stage back to the top.

plain.title: You tap the side rail
plain.detail: The rail tells the conductor which screen you want, and scrolls back to the top.

steps.title: App swaps the screen component
steps.detail: page state indexes a plain screens map { Home, Topics, Projects, Notes, About }. The key={page} on the rendered screen forces a fresh mount and the fade-in.

plain.title: The conductor swaps screens
plain.detail: It changes one remembered word — Home, Topics, Projects — and shows the matching screen. Like changing channels; the address bar never moves.

steps.title: Global attributes are rewritten
steps.detail: An effect sets data-fit (native on Home/Topics, fluid elsewhere), data-traymat, data-tilemat and friends on <html> — screens change their material by cascade, not by prop drilling.

plain.title: App-wide switches are rewritten
plain.detail: Labels for material and fit are set on the page. Screens change appearance through the stylesheet rather than being told individually.

steps.title: The tray screen renders
steps.detail: HomeTray (two glide shelves) or TopicsTray (4×2 grid) mounts inside the fixed 980×612 canvas.

plain.title: The screen appears
plain.detail: Home’s shelves or the Topics grid mounts inside the fixed-size canvas and fades in.

steps.title: Content comes from constants
steps.detail: ZMATH_TOPICS and ZMATH_PROJECTS drive the tiles; ById maps resolve a selection back to its record. Nothing is fetched.

plain.title: Content comes from the content file
plain.detail: Topics and projects are read straight from the file. Nothing is fetched.

steps.title: Cover art by reference
steps.detail: Each tile's art is a <use href> into the single injected <defs> block, so eight covers cost one copy of the geometry.

plain.title: Artwork by reference
plain.detail: Each tile points at one stored copy of its cover art rather than carrying its own.

steps.title: Second tap opens the modal
steps.detail: Lab tap rhythm — first tap rings the selection, second calls onOpen({type,data}); App stores it as entry and the shared Modal in components.jsx renders it.

plain.title: A second tap opens it
plain.detail: First tap highlights, second tap opens the pop-up panel. On a touch screen with no hover, that lets you look before you leap.

plain.label: Tapping through the app
plain.summary: How a tap on the side rail or a tile becomes a new screen.

flows.label: Fixed-canvas tray scaling
flows.summary: The defining layout decision: screens are drawn once at a logical size and scaled like a TV picture, not reflowed.

steps.title: Viewport → CSS variables
steps.detail: A resize listener writes --ipad-scale = min(w/1180, h/820) and --hd-scale = min(w/1920, h/1080) onto <html> for the fixed canvases the shell chrome uses.

plain.title: The window is measured
plain.detail: The app works out how much room it has and writes it down as a simple multiplier.

steps.title: useFit measures the tray
steps.detail: A ResizeObserver on .lab-stage measures the padded box each frame it changes — the tray footprint, not the window.

plain.title: The tray is measured, not the window
plain.detail: What matters is the space the tray itself has, so that is watched directly.

steps.title: scale = min(w/980, h/612, 1.6)
steps.detail: The 980×612 design scales up to fill, but the 1.6× cap stops growth on large monitors so the tray centers with margin instead of ballooning.

plain.title: Scale up — but only so far
plain.detail: The design grows to fill the space, then stops at about 1.6 times its natural size and centres with margin. Without the cap, a big monitor would inflate the tiles absurdly.

steps.title: heroScale → .scr → tiles
steps.detail: heroScale is sized cw×scale in real pixels; .scr keeps the logical size and carries transform: scale(). Tiles are direct children of .scr — the TRAY-CONTAINMENT RULE — so tray and tiles are one scaling unit.

plain.title: Tray and tiles scale together
plain.detail: The tiles sit inside the tray, so the whole picture zooms as one unit. Separate them and they drift out of alignment at some window sizes.

steps.title: The Lab uses the same recipe
steps.detail: LabSpotlight was the original; Home and Topics were ported onto its shell pattern so all three trays behave identically.

plain.title: The Lab does exactly the same
plain.detail: Home and Topics were modelled on it, so all three screens behave identically.

steps.title: Fixed logical geometry
steps.detail: Tiles 218×162, cartridges 294×162, gaps 16 — all in canvas units. The full-screen peek (5th tile, 4th cartridge sliver) is a consequence of these fixed numbers, not a media query.

plain.title: Fixed sizes, not window rules
plain.detail: A tile is always the same size. The sliver of the next tile you see at full width falls out of those numbers — it says there is more to scroll to, without an arrow.

steps.title: Material inherited
steps.detail: Both tray sheets are scoped under .lab-spot and read the base tile material from lab.css, so a material change lands on all three screens at once.

plain.title: One material, shared
plain.detail: Both tray screens inherit their base look from the Lab, so a material change lands on all three at once.

plain.label: Why nothing ever rearranges
plain.summary: Screens are drawn once at a fixed size and scaled like a photo, instead of reflowing.

flows.label: Note figures — registry pattern
flows.summary: How a string in a data file becomes a rendered SVG diagram without any load-order fragility.

steps.title: A note body is an array of blocks
steps.detail: ZMATH_NOTES entries carry body blocks — { sec }, { p }, { fig: 'name' } — plus inline exercises with answers and solutions.

plain.title: An article is a list of pieces
plain.detail: A heading, some paragraphs, a diagram named “lattice”, more paragraphs — all typed into the content file.

steps.title: NotesScreen renders the article
steps.detail: Reading state slides the list pane out and the reader pane in; each body block is handed to NoteBlock.

plain.title: The article is laid out
plain.detail: The list pane slides away, the reader slides in, and each piece is handed off to be drawn.

steps.title: NoteBlock dispatches on block shape
steps.detail: For { fig: 'name' } it looks up ZFIGURES[name] and renders the component it finds.

plain.title: Each piece is looked at in turn
plain.detail: A paragraph is printed. A diagram name is looked up on the shared hook.

steps.title: One registry object, one owner
steps.detail: figures-registry.js exports a single empty object. It replaced window.ZFIGURES so the import graph — not script order — decides who populates it.

plain.title: The coat check
plain.detail: One shared list with one clear owner. Nothing depends on files loading in a particular order — which is what the old approach got wrong.

steps.title: Figures self-register on import
steps.detail: components.jsx imports figures.jsx purely for the side-effect; each diagram adds itself to ZFIGURES, and components.jsx adds its own 'parallelogram'. Arrows point one way.

plain.title: Diagrams hang themselves up
plain.detail: Each diagram adds itself to the list when the app starts. Adding a new one needs no changes anywhere else.

plain.label: How a lesson diagram appears
plain.summary: How a word in an article becomes a drawing on the page — the coat-check idea.

flows.label: Tweaks → live restyling
flows.summary: The design-time control surface, and how a toggle becomes a cascade change.

steps.title: Defaults live in a marked block
steps.detail: TWEAK_DEFAULTS sits between EDITMODE-BEGIN/END comments in app.jsx so the host can rewrite it on disk — the values persist as source, not as browser storage.

plain.title: Settings live in the source
plain.detail: Default choices sit in a marked block in the code, so they persist as source rather than in the browser.

steps.title: useTweaks holds the values
steps.detail: A single state object; setTweak accepts either a key/value pair or a patch object, and notifies the host to persist.

plain.title: The panel holds the current values
plain.detail: Flip a control and the new value is saved back into that block.

steps.title: An effect writes data-* on <html>
steps.detail: data-material, data-fit, data-tilemat, data-traymat, data-ambience, data-energy, data-capsule — one effect, re-run on tweak or page change.

plain.title: A label is written onto the page
plain.detail: Something like “material: flat.” That is all the code does.

steps.title: CSS reacts, React does not re-render
steps.detail: tweaks-overrides.css is last in the chain and keys off those attributes, so a material switch is a pure cascade change with no component churn.

plain.title: The stylesheet reacts
plain.detail: It is watching for those labels and restyles accordingly. Nothing is rebuilt: code decides the state, the stylesheet decides the look.

steps.title: Tokens do the actual work
steps.detail: Overrides mostly reassign token variables, so one attribute flip repaints every surface that reads them.

plain.title: Named values do the real work
plain.detail: Most switches just reassign colours and sizes, so one flip repaints every surface using them.

plain.label: Changing the look instantly
plain.summary: How one switch repaints the whole app without rebuilding anything.

flows.label: Device gates — phone & orientation
flows.summary: Two guards, both owned by the brain so the shells cannot drift apart.

steps.title: Phone gate is pure CSS
steps.detail: Under 700px wide (or 500px tall) #root is hidden and a notice shows. No JS, no React — it works before a single module has loaded. Kept identical in both shells.

plain.title: Phones are turned away by styling alone
plain.detail: Below a certain width the app is hidden and a notice shows. No code involved — it works before anything has loaded.

steps.title: RotateGuard is portalled to <body>
steps.detail: createPortal places the overlay outside #root deliberately, so a CSS rule can hide the app behind it.

plain.title: The rotate notice sits above everything
plain.detail: It is placed outside the app’s normal container deliberately, so it can cover the whole page.

steps.title: body:has(#rotate-guard) #root { display:none }
steps.detail: In portrait the guard exists and the app is hidden by selector alone. Living in the brain means both readers get the same guard from one source.

plain.title: One rule hides the app behind it
plain.detail: When the notice exists, the app is hidden. A single line of styling, no code juggling.

steps.title: Reduced motion respected
steps.detail: A matchMedia check adds .reduce-motion to <body> on mount, letting the whole animation layer stand down from CSS.

plain.title: Motion preferences are respected
plain.detail: If your device asks for reduced motion, the app marks the page and the animations stand down.

plain.label: Blocking the wrong device
plain.summary: Two checks that stop the app on a phone, or when the tablet is held the wrong way.

observations.title: Shared core, thin adapters
observations.detail: All logic in zmath/; both shells are adapters. Duplication is structurally impossible because there is exactly one copy of the source.

plain.title: One brain, two readers
plain.detail: All the code lives in one folder; both ways of opening the app point at it. Duplication is impossible because there is only one copy.

observations.title: Routing by state, not by URL
observations.detail: A screens map indexed by a page string. URL params exist only as optional deep-link overrides (?page=, ?fit=) used by comparison harnesses.

plain.title: Screens change like channels
plain.detail: The app remembers a word and shows the matching screen. No web addresses, no back-button expectations.

observations.title: Attribute-driven theming
observations.detail: React writes data-* attributes on <html>; CSS owns every visual consequence. Material changes cost no re-render.

plain.title: Flip a switch, do not repaint
plain.detail: Code sets a label; the stylesheet decides what it looks like. Appearance changes cost nothing.

observations.title: Fixed canvas, uniform scale
observations.detail: 980×612 (trays), 1180×820 (iPad), 1920×1080 (HD) — scaled, never reflowed. Layout bugs are geometry bugs, not breakpoint bugs.

plain.title: Drawn once, then scaled
plain.detail: Fixed sizes scaled like a photo, never reflowed. Layout problems are measurement problems, not window-size problems.

observations.title: Registry over globals
observations.detail: figures-registry.js gives the figure table one importable owner, eliminating script-order dependence.

plain.title: A coat check, not a pile
plain.detail: Diagrams hang themselves up by name, so nothing depends on the order files happen to load in.

observations.title: figkit.jsx is detached
observations.detail: Converted to ESM but imported by nothing — it does not load at runtime. Wire it in or retire it.

plain.title: A tool nobody picks up
plain.detail: One file of diagram parts is referenced by nothing and never loads. It looks alive, which wastes a future reader’s time. Wire it in or delete it.

observations.title: CDN dependency at boot
observations.detail: The live reader needs unpkg (Babel) and esm.sh (React) at load time. Offline or blocked, the page shows the loader's error panel.

plain.title: Needs the internet to start
plain.detail: The live version fetches the translator and the toolkit at startup. Offline, it shows an error instead of an app. The packaged build does not have this problem.

observations.title: Compile cost on every load
observations.detail: The no-build reader re-fetches and re-compiles the whole graph per page load. Fine for a study build; the Vite output is the answer for production.

plain.title: Re-translated on every load
plain.detail: The live version redoes the whole translation each time it opens. Fine while building; the packaged build is the answer for real use.

observations.title: No backend
observations.detail: No API, no database, no auth, no persistence beyond the host-written EDITMODE block. Content ships as constants in data.js.

plain.title: Nothing is stored anywhere
plain.detail: No server, no database, no login. All content is typed into the app itself.

$note: Single source of truth for the project architecture. Every layer, node, flow, step, observation, glossary term, invariant and behaviour carries a `plain` twin — technical text is the default field, `plain` is the same meaning in non-specialist English. Sections: layers · nodes · edges · flows · observations · invariants (rules that must not break) · glossary (the vocabulary, linked to the nodes that demonstrate it) · behaviours (things that look like bugs but are decisions). Pages read this file; they never restate it.

invariants.title: Edit only inside the brain
invariants.condition: No application source exists outside AlphabetMath - Mobile/zmath/. AlphabetMath - App/src/main.jsx contains imports only.
invariants.breaks: The two readers diverge silently. A fix lands in one and not the other, and months later a bug exists in only one version with no record of which is correct.

plain.title: Edit only inside the brain
plain.condition: All real code lives in zmath. The packaged version holds no app code at all.
plain.breaks: The two versions quietly disagree, and you cannot tell which one is right.

invariants.title: Tray and tiles are one scaling unit
invariants.condition: Tiles are direct children of .scr. Structure is lab-stage → heroScale → .scr → tiles, with no intermediate wrapper between .scr and the tiles.
invariants.breaks: Tiles drift out of alignment with the tray at some window sizes, because two elements end up scaled by two different measurements.
invariants.note: Resizing tile or cartridge dimensions is fine and does not affect this rule.

plain.title: Tray and tiles scale together
plain.condition: The tiles sit inside the tray, so the whole picture zooms as one.
plain.breaks: The tiles slide out of place at some window sizes and the illusion collapses.

invariants.title: New styling is added to styles.css, never to a shell
invariants.condition: Both shells reference exactly one stylesheet. Every other sheet is reached by @import from styles.css.
invariants.breaks: A sheet added to one shell is absent from the other, so the two readers look different.

plain.title: New styling goes on one list
plain.condition: Both ways of opening the app load one stylesheet, which pulls in the rest.
plain.breaks: Styling added to a page would be missing from the other version.

invariants.title: Screens are scaled, not reflowed
invariants.condition: Screen geometry is expressed in canvas units at a fixed logical size and fitted with a single uniform transform. No media queries reposition tray content.
invariants.breaks: Elements move relative to each other at different window sizes, breaking the physical-object illusion the visual identity rests on.

plain.title: Screens are pictures, not layouts
plain.condition: Drawn once at a fixed size and scaled like a photo.
plain.breaks: Things start moving around when the window changes, and it stops feeling like an object.

invariants.title: Content is compiled in, never fetched
invariants.condition: All topics, projects, notes, article bodies and exercises are constants in data.js. No fetch, no API, no database, no persistence beyond the host-written EDITMODE block.
invariants.breaks: Introducing a fetch adds a loading state, a failure state and a server — the three things this architecture exists to avoid.

plain.title: Content is typed in, not fetched
plain.condition: Every topic, note and exercise sits in one content file.
plain.breaks: Adding a server brings back loading spinners, error states, and something to maintain.

invariants.title: Appearance is switches, not instructions
invariants.condition: React writes data-* attributes on <html>; CSS owns every visual consequence. Components are never handed per-instance appearance props.
invariants.breaks: Appearance changes start costing re-renders, and you can no longer tell whether a look is decided in code or in CSS.

plain.title: Appearance is switches, not instructions
plain.condition: Code sets a label; the stylesheet decides what it looks like.
plain.breaks: Styling problems become impossible to locate, because they could be in either place.

glossary.detail: The single source folder, zmath/. Both shells resolve into it; no source exists outside it.

plain.detail: The one folder holding all the real code. Everything else points at it.

glossary.detail: A host document plus whatever it needs to start the brain. Contains no application logic.

plain.detail: A wrapper that knows how to start the brain. There are two.

glossary.detail: A module whose entire body is imports pointing elsewhere. Zero logic, so nothing can drift.

plain.detail: A file that contains no logic of its own — it just connects one thing to another.

glossary.detail: One source file with its own scope, declaring what it needs and what it offers.

plain.detail: One source file. The import graph is the web of which files call for which others.

glossary.detail: The directed graph of module dependencies. The loader walks it depth-first; Vite resolves it at build time.

plain.detail: The web of which files call for which others.

glossary.detail: A declaration that one module needs a binding from another.

plain.detail: One file saying: I need something from that other file.

glossary.detail: An import by package name rather than by path — react, not ./react.js. Resolved by the import map here, by node_modules in Vite, both pointing at the same version. That is what keeps one source set valid in both readers.

plain.detail: Asking for something by name instead of by location.

glossary.detail: Compiling and bundling source before it can run. The live reader has none; the Vite reader does it ahead of time.

plain.detail: Preparing and packaging code before anyone can run it. The live version does not have one.

glossary.detail: Converting JSX into plain JavaScript — in the browser via Babel-standalone, or at build time via Vite.

plain.detail: Translating the source dialect into something the browser understands.

glossary.detail: An in-memory URL standing in for a file. The loader rewrites each module to point at its dependencies blob URLs, which is how a no-build import graph resolves.

plain.detail: A temporary address for something held in memory rather than saved to disk.

glossary.detail: The first module executed. Everything else is reached from it. Both shells converge on main.jsx.

plain.detail: The first file that runs. Everything else is reached from it.

glossary.detail: A value React re-renders on when it changes. Here: which page you are on, which modal is open, the tweak values.

plain.detail: Something the app is currently remembering — such as which screen you are on.

glossary.detail: A function returning UI, with its own props and behaviour. A tile is one.

plain.detail: A reusable piece of interface with its own appearance and behaviour. A tile is one.

glossary.detail: Producing a components output and inserting it into the document for the first time.

plain.detail: Drawing a component onto the screen for the first time.

glossary.detail: Deriving what to show from the URL. Deliberately absent — a screens map keyed by a page string does the job instead.

plain.detail: Using the web address to decide what to show. This app deliberately does not do it.

glossary.detail: A single exported object that other modules populate on import and a consumer reads by key. Replaces load-order-dependent globals.

plain.detail: The coat check — a shared list things add themselves to so others can find them by name.

glossary.detail: Work a module performs merely by being imported, rather than through anything it exports.

plain.detail: A file that does something merely by being loaded, rather than by being called.

glossary.detail: Content compiled into the bundle as constants. No fetch, no API, no database.

plain.detail: Content typed into the app itself instead of fetched from a server.

glossary.detail: The CSS rule that later declarations of equal specificity win. Here the @import order in styles.css is a deliberate hierarchy of authority.

plain.detail: The rule that later styling can override earlier styling. Why sheet order matters.

glossary.detail: A CSS custom property holding a named design value. Overrides mostly reassign tokens, so one flip repaints everything reading them.

plain.detail: A named value — a colour, a size — referred to by name, so one edit changes everything using it.

glossary.detail: Authoring at one logical size and applying a uniform transform: scale() to fit, instead of reflowing. Layout bugs become geometry bugs.

plain.detail: Designing at one exact size and scaling the result, rather than letting it reflow.

glossary.detail: Content rearranging at breakpoints to fit the viewport. Standard on the web; avoided here because it would break the physical-object illusion.

plain.detail: Content rearranging itself to fit the window. Standard on the web; avoided here.

glossary.detail: The visible area of the window. Measured here to derive a scale, never to switch layouts.

plain.detail: The visible area of the window.

glossary.detail: A React component that catches render errors below it and renders a fallback — here, the real stack in monospace.

plain.detail: The safety net that prints a real error instead of showing a blank white screen.

glossary.detail: A check that blocks the app until a condition holds. The phone gate is pure CSS; the rotate guard is a portalled overlay plus one selector.

plain.detail: A check that blocks the app until a condition is met — correct screen size, correct orientation.

glossary.detail: Rendering into a DOM node outside the components own tree. Used so the rotate overlay sits outside #root and a CSS rule can hide the app behind it.

plain.detail: Placing something outside the apps normal container, so it can sit over the top of everything.

glossary.detail: A server the client talks to. This project has none, by choice.

plain.detail: A server the app talks to. This project has none, by choice.

behaviours.title: Tiles need two taps
behaviours.observed: First tap rings and selects the tile. A second tap on the same tile calls onOpen and the modal appears.
behaviours.deliberate: Touch screens have no hover, so there is no way to inspect before committing. The ring is the hover state, made explicit.
behaviours.mistaken_fix: Making the first tap open the modal — which removes the look-before-you-leap step and makes every mis-tap costly.

plain.observed: Tap once to highlight, tap again to open.
plain.deliberate: On a touch screen there is no hovering, so this is your chance to look before you leap.
plain.mistaken_fix: Making one tap open it. Then every mis-tap costs you a pop-up.

behaviours.title: A half tile shows at the edge
behaviours.observed: At full width the shelf shows a partial fifth tile (or fourth cartridge) clipped at the right edge.
behaviours.deliberate: It falls out of the fixed tile geometry rather than a media query, and it signals that the shelf continues — an affordance costing no scrollbar and no arrow.
behaviours.mistaken_fix: Adjusting tile width or gap so the row ends cleanly — which removes the only cue that there is more to scroll to.

plain.observed: At full width you see a sliver of the next tile.
plain.deliberate: It tells you the shelf keeps going, without needing a scrollbar or an arrow.
plain.mistaken_fix: Resizing the tiles so the row ends neatly — and losing the only hint that there is more.

behaviours.title: No internet, no app
behaviours.observed: The live reader fetches Babel from unpkg and React from esm.sh at startup. Offline or blocked, the loader prints its error panel instead of the app.
behaviours.deliberate: Accepted cost of having no build step. The Vite build carries everything and exists partly for this reason.
behaviours.mistaken_fix: Vendoring the CDN files into the brain folder — which reintroduces the copies-that-drift problem the whole structure avoids. Use the packaged build instead.

plain.observed: With no connection, the live version shows an error instead of an app.
plain.deliberate: That is the price of having no publishing step. The packaged version carries everything with it.
plain.mistaken_fix: Copying those files into the project — which brings back the two-copies problem. Use the packaged build.
